questions.question_text: State the domain and range of $y=\arcsin x$.

options.why: Gives the domain and range of restricted sine instead of its inverse.
Uses the range of inverse cosine instead of inverse sine.
Excludes the endpoints, although inverse sine is defined at both $x=-1$ and $x=1$.

questions.question_text: State the domain and range of $y=\arctan x$.

options.why: Includes the asymptote values, which inverse tangent never reaches.
Uses the domain restriction of inverse sine and inverse cosine.
Gives the domain and range of restricted tangent instead of its inverse.

questions.question_text: Which statement is true of the graph of $y=\arcsin x$?

options.text: It is increasing and it is an odd function.
It is decreasing and it is an odd function.
options.why: Took the decreasing behaviour of $y=\arccos x$; restricted sine rises, so its inverse rises too.

options.text: It is increasing and it is an even function.
options.why: Claims $\arcsin(-x)=\arcsin x$; in fact $\arcsin(-x)=-\arcsin x$.

options.text: It is decreasing and it is an even function.
options.why: Confuses $y=\arcsin x$ with $y=\arccos x$ on both counts, and $\arccos$ is not even either.

questions.solution_text:
$y=\sin x$ increases on $-\frac{\pi}{2}\le x\le\frac{\pi}{2}$, and reflecting in $y=x$ keeps a curve increasing.
$\arcsin(-x)=-\arcsin x$, which is the condition for an odd function.
The graph is increasing and odd.

questions.question_text: Which statement about the notation $\tan^{-1}x$ is correct?

options.text: It is the inverse function of the restricted tangent, so its output is an angle.
It is the reciprocal $\frac{1}{\tan x}$, so its output is a ratio.
options.why: Reads the $-1$ as an index; the reciprocal of $\tan x$ is written $\cot x$, not $\tan^{-1}x$.

options.text: It is the reciprocal $\frac{1}{\tan x}$, so its output is an angle.
options.why: Reads the $-1$ as an index, and a reciprocal of a ratio is a ratio, not an angle.

options.text: It is the inverse function of the restricted tangent, so its output is a ratio.
options.why: Identifies the function correctly but not its output; an inverse trig function returns the angle, not the ratio.

questions.solution_text:
The $-1$ in $\tan^{-1}x$ marks an inverse function, not a power.
The restricted tangent takes an angle and returns a ratio, so its inverse takes a ratio and returns an angle.
It is the inverse function of the restricted tangent, so its output is an angle.

questions.question_text: Which statement is true of the graph of $y=\arctan x$?

options.text: It is increasing and it is an odd function.
It is decreasing and it is an odd function.
options.why: Uses the decreasing behaviour of inverse cosine instead of the increasing behaviour of inverse tangent.

options.text: It is increasing and it is an even function.
options.why: Claims equal outputs at opposite inputs; inverse tangent has opposite outputs at opposite inputs.

options.text: It is decreasing and it is neither odd nor even.
options.why: Uses the properties of inverse cosine instead of inverse tangent.

questions.question_text: By swapping $x$ and $y$, find the inverse of $y=2+\sin x$ for $-\frac{\pi}{2}\le x\le\frac{\pi}{2}$.

options.why: Added $2$ instead of subtracting it when making $\sin y$ the subject.
Applied $\arcsin$ before undoing the $+2$, so the subtraction ended up outside the inverse function.
Left the $+2$ outside the inverse function and did not change its sign.

questions.question_text: Which statement is true of the graph of $y=\arccos x$?

options.text: It is decreasing, and it is neither odd nor even.
It is decreasing, and it is an odd function.
options.why: Copies the oddness of $y=\arcsin x$; $\arccos(-x)=\pi-\arccos x$, which is not $-\arccos x$.

options.text: It is increasing, and it is neither odd nor even.
options.why: Restricted cosine falls from $1$ to $-1$ on $[0,\pi]$, so its inverse falls as well.

options.text: It is increasing, and it is an odd function.
options.why: Confuses $y=\arccos x$ with $y=\arcsin x$ on both counts.

questions.solution_text:
$y=\cos x$ decreases on $0\le x\le\pi$, and reflecting in $y=x$ keeps a curve decreasing.
$\arccos 0=\frac{\pi}{2}$, which is not $0$, so the graph is not symmetric about the origin and is not odd.
$\arccos(-1)=\pi$ but $\arccos 1=0$, so it is not even either.
It is decreasing, and it is neither odd nor even.

questions.question_text: By swapping $x$ and $y$, find the inverse of $y=5-2\sin\left(\frac{x}{4}\right)$ for $-2\pi\le x\le2\pi$.

options.why: Divides by $2$ instead of $-2$ when rearranging $x-5=-2\sin(y/4)$.
Divides by $4$ instead of multiplying by $4$ when solving for $y$.
Multiplies $x$ by $2$ instead of dividing the whole expression $5-x$ by $2$.
This is the correct principal range for inverse sine.
This is the correct principal range for inverse cosine.
The output range of arccos remains from zero to pi when defined.

questions.solution_text: The principal range of $\arctan x$ is strict: $-\pi/2<\arctan x<\pi/2$. It never reaches the endpoints, so the inclusive inequality in B is incorrect.
